nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NiFe2O4
nodes.procedure: 0.4754 g of NiCl₂·6H₂O and 1.1119 g of FeSO₄·7H₂O were dissolved in a mixed solution of 40 mL of deionized water and 60 mL of ethylene glycol, and then 4 mL of ammonia solution was injected. The resulting mixture was stirred vigorously for 1 h, and then poured into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. The autoclave was heated to and maintained at 180 °C for 24 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the NiFe₂O₄ precipitate was separated from the autoclave using external magnet and washed with ethyl alcohol and deionized water for three times. Finally, the particles were dried in oven at 60 °C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Coprecipitation synthesis of NiFe2O4/ZnAl-EDTA LDH
nodes.procedure: Firstly, CO₂-free water was prepared by purging N₂ into deionized water for 30 min under nitrogen flow in water bath at 60 °C, and the CO₂-free water was used throughout the whole preparation process. Prepared NiFe₂O₄ was ultrasonically dispersed into 150 mL CO₂-free water for 15 min to obtain uniform suspension, then transferred into 500 mL four-neck round flask for continuous mechanical agitation in water bath at 60 °C under nitrogen atmosphere protection. Meanwhile, salt solution (100 mL) containing 7.4373 g Zn(NO₃)₂·6H₂O and 4.6891 g Al(NO₃)₃·9H₂O (Zn/Al molar ratio = 2) was dropwise added, and alkaline solution (100 mL) containing 4.00 g NaOH (1 M) and 0.74458 g Na₂EDTA (0.02 M) added simultaneously to maintain pH at 10.5±0.2. After complete addition, slurry aged for 8 h, washed with deionized water until neutral supernatant, magnetically separated, dried at 60 °C overnight, and ground into fine powder.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH exhibits irregular surface structure and flake-like morphology (Fig. 2c); after Cr(VI) adsorption shows more compact surface (Fig. 2d).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Unlike NiFe₂O₄ and ZnAl-EDTA LDH, the SEM image of NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH as shown in Fig. 2c exhibits an irregular surface structure and a flake-like morphology. After adsorption of Cr(VI), the hybrid magnetic adsorbent shows a more compact surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH shows morphology like attachment of black tiny NiFe₂O₄ particles on ZnAl-EDTA LDH layer surface (Fig. 2e).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image of Fig. 2e shows that the morphology of NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH looks like an attachment of black tiny NiFe₂O₄ particles on the surface of ZnAl-EDTA LDH layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄ and NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH are super-paramagnetic with saturation magnetization values of 56.72 emu/g and 5.93 emu/g respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It shows that both NiFe₂O₄ and NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH are essentially super-paramagnetic, and magnetization saturation value of them are 56.72 and 5.93 emu g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄ shows cubic spinel structure with diffractions at 18.50°, 30.28°, 35.62° etc.; ZnAl-EDTA LDH shows hydrotalcite peaks at 11.86° (003), 23.88° (006) etc.; NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH shows weaker peaks indicating poor crystallinity but no impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns were conducted to identify the phase structure ... no peaks of any other impurities are detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄ shows Fe-O at 582 cm⁻¹; ZnAl-EDTA LDH shows O-H at 3440 cm⁻¹, C=O at 1601 cm⁻¹, C-OH at 1384 cm⁻¹, N-H at 1111 cm⁻¹; all characteristic peaks present in composite.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR spectrum are shown in Fig. 3b to identify the type of functional groups ... all these characteristic absorption peaks originated from NiFe₂O₄ and EDTA²⁻ can be found in the spectrum.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption/desorption isotherms show type IV curves with H3 hysteresis; NiFe₂O₄: 14.972 m²/g, 0.110 cm³/g, 30.074 nm; ZnAl-EDTA LDH: 2.023 m²/g, 0.011 cm³/g, 3.823 nm; NiFe₂O₄/ZnAl-EDTA LDH: 1.518 m²/g, 0.009 cm³/g, 4.074 nm; all mesoporous.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherms ... revealing the mesoporous structure of the adsorbents.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s shows M-O at 530.6 eV, -OH at 531.8 eV, C=O at 532.35 eV, H₂O at 532.6 eV; after Cr(VI) adsorption C=O and -OH peaks decrease; Cr 2p shows Cr(VI) at 579.2/588.3 eV and Cr(III) at 577.4/586.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution spectrum of O 1s ... It indicates the existence of both Cr(VI) and Cr(III) on the surface.
